steelworks-guide-getting-started-text: Getting started Begin with steel ingot and Expanded Matter² crushed ore. A pulverizer is needed for many blend ingredients. The advanced furnace produces blister steel and specialty metals in eight reusable cavities. Earlier metals Cupronickel uses normal alloy smelting. Iron Blend also produces cast iron in a crucible. Cast iron tools are limited to the previously supported cast tools and anvil. Next steps Furnace construction • Metal production
steelworks-guide-construction-text: Construction Build a 3×3×6 structure using intact refractory bricks. The following layers are ordered from bottom to top. Layer 1 — Foundation A complete 3×3 refractory brick base. Layer 2 — Lower fuel chamber Place an outward-facing refractory air intake in at least one side center, with coke in the center. Fill the remaining wall positions with bricks. Layer 3 — Upper fuel chamber Place a steel fuel hatch at any side center. Coke occupies the center. Layer 4 — Grating Place native refractory grating in the center; surround it with bricks. Layer 5 — Alloy container Place the reusable alloy container in the center; surround it with bricks. Layer 6 — Loading hatch Place the loading hatch in the center; surround it with bricks. Structure preview On the intake, use shift + right-click to show missing or incorrect blocks, and shift + ctrl + right-click to hide the preview. Default temperature limits Tier 1: 1500°C Tier 2: 1650°C Tier 3: 1800°C The weakest refractory component sets the limit. Server settings can change the limits; inspect the assembled furnace for its current limit. Furnace operation
steelworks-guide-operation-text: Firing Open the fuel hatch. Sneak + right-click with coke to load fuel, then ignite with a firestarter. The furnace can preheat without blends. Natural draft is available without bellows: one unobstructed intake supplies 30%, two 50%, three 70%, and four 90% airflow by default. Active bellows can supply up to 100%. Server settings can change these values. Close both hatches to retain heat. Loading Open the loading hatch. Sneak + right-click with the desired blend. Only one blend type per batch; load in multiples of 20, up to 160. Each mold holds the equivalent of 20 blends. Close both hatches to process. Watching the batch The native-style dynamic renderer shows the blend, temperature glow, molten metal and hardened ingots. Processing advances only above the recipe temperature. Fuel automatically stops at completion; to stop manually, open the fuel hatch and sneak + right-click with an empty hand. Retrieving ingots When the metal has hardened, sneak + right-click with a hammer once to release the batch. Use metal tongs to retrieve ingots at 200°C or hotter; collect cooler ingots by hand. Reheat for smithing if necessary. Related information Metal production • Furnace maintenance
steelworks-guide-materials-text: Blends Each recipe yields four blends; each blend represents five metal units. Twenty blends produce one ingot, up to eight ingots per batch. Crushed coal is an additive; coke is the furnace fuel. Iron Blend 4 crushed iron + 1 crushed coal. Crucible: cast iron at 1320°C. Furnace: blister steel at 1450°C for 8 hours, tier 1. Refine blister steel on an anvil. Nickel steel 3 crushed iron + 2 crushed nickel + 1 crushed coal. 1550°C for 12 hours, tier 2. Stainless steel 3 crushed iron + 1 crushed nickel + 1 crushed chromite + 1 crushed coal. 1600°C for 18 hours, tier 2. Chrome steel 4 crushed iron + 1 crushed chromite + 1 crushed coal. 1625°C for 18 hours, tier 2. Titanium 4 powdered titanium dioxide + 1 crushed coal. 1750°C for 24 hours, tier 3. This is simplified gameplay refining. Processing time These are default in-game hours at operating temperature. Heating and cooling take additional time; the server configuration can change processing temperatures, durations and speed. Inspect the loaded furnace for its effective recipe temperature and remaining time. Listed tiers assume default temperature limits. Equipment balance Nominal durability relative to equivalent vanilla steel: cupronickel 80%, cast iron 90% (limited equipment), nickel steel 135%, chrome steel 150%, stainless steel 165%, titanium 200%. Chrome steel retains higher weapon damage than stainless steel. Actual item values depend on equipment family, optional mods and server overrides. Stainless steel favors long service life; chrome steel favors damage, mining speed and stronger armor protection.
steelworks-guide-smithing-text: Smithing Use a native forge and anvil to shape the ingots into heads and equipment. Cupronickel requires bronze or better; specialty steels require iron or better; titanium requires steel or equivalent. Cast iron anvil sections are an exception to the limited cast-tool policy. Quenching Nickel steel, stainless steel, chrome steel and titanium use the native Quenchable behavior on eligible tool heads and directly forged tools. Heat the item into its displayed quenching range (default 815–1050°C), use tongs, and cool in water. Native accumulated treatment effects apply. Default shatter-risk increments relative to vanilla steel: nickel steel 65%, stainless steel 30%, chrome steel 45%, titanium 2%. Server settings can change these values. Use fire clay coverage where the native recipe permits it. Tempering After quenching, eligible pieces display their tempering range (default 550–700°C). Reheat and temper using the native game interaction. Assemble the finished head with its handle; native recipes transfer supported treatment buffs to the tool. Cast iron and cupronickel do not use these steel heat-treatment rules. Equipment Metal tongs, crowbars, wrenches, helve hammer heads, arrowheads, armor components and shield components are forged on an anvil. Assemble them with the normal native recipes. Armor and round shields use the native protection system. Anvils All six Steelworks anvils can be forged in two parts. Cast iron and cupronickel may also be cast in an anvil mold. Use the normal native weld process for forged parts. Optional Toolsmith integration (experimental) Additional binding materials and multipart model overrides are provided for Toolsmith 1.2.20. Heat-treatment transfer through Toolsmith assembly, sharpening and recovery is not yet verified.
steelworks-guide-maintenance-text: Refractory wear Default check interval is 168 operating game hours above 1340°C. Per check: tier 1 10%, tier 2 5%, tier 3 0.1%. Bricks, gratings and air intakes may degrade; replace damaged parts. The alloy container does not degrade. Server settings can disable degradation or change the interval and chances. Troubleshooting No heat: verify fuel, structure, hatches and airflow. No progress: check recipe temperature, tier and loaded blend quantity. No release: allow the metal to harden first. Use the intake preview to diagnose missing or incorrect blocks.
advanced-steelmaking-text: From crushed ore to advanced alloys Getting started Steelworks requires Expanded Matter². Begin with vanilla steelmaking, then construct an advanced alloy furnace to produce specialty steels and titanium. Construction Build a 3×3×6 refractory furnace, using an air intake, fuel hatch, grating, alloy container and loading hatch. Furnace construction explains each layer. Operation Use coke as fuel and crushed coal in blends. Preheat the chamber, use unobstructed intakes for natural draft or active bellows for forced draft, and load up to 160 blends. See Furnace operation. Metal production Metal production covers the recipes, temperature limits and processing durations. Working the metal Smithing and heat treatment explains forging, casting, quenching, tempering, armor and shields. Maintenance Furnace maintenance explains refractory wear and troubleshooting.
